title: Network pharmacology of triptolide in cancer cells: implications for transcription factor binding.
authors: Seo, Ean-Jeong; Dawood, Mona; Hult, Annika K; Olsson, Martin L; Efferth, Thomas
one_liner_zh: 该文结合转录组分析与分子对接研究雷公藤甲素对NF-kB和GATA1转录因子结合的影响，涉及TF-DNA结合位点富集分析，但核心是药物作用机制而非TF-DNA互作建模，方法以实验和简单对接为主，深度有限。
abstract: Background Triptolide is an active natural product, which inhibits cell proliferation, induces cell apoptosis, suppresses tumor metastasis and improves the effect of other therapeutic treatments in several cancer cell lines by affecting multiple molecules and signaling pathways, such as caspases, heat-shock proteins, DNA damage and NF-kB. Purpose We investigated the effect of triptolide towards NF-kB and GATA1. Methods We used cell viability assay, compare and cluster analyses of microarray-based mRNA transcriptome-wide expression data, gene promoter binding motif analysis, molecular docking, Ingenuity pathway analysis, NF-kB reporter cell assay, and electrophoretic mobility shift assay (EMSA) of GATA1. Results Triptolide inhibited the growth of drug-sensitive (CCRF-CEM, U87.MG) and drug-resistant cell lines (CEM/ADR5000, U87.MGDeltaEGFR). Hierarchical cluster analysis showed six major clusters in dendrogram. The sensitive and resistant cell lines were statistically significant (p = 0.65 x 10(-2)) distributed. The binding motifs of NF-kappaB (Rel) and of GATA1 proteins were significantly enriched in regions of 25 kb upstream promoter of all genes. IPA showed the networks, biological functions, and canonical pathways influencing the activity of triptolide towards tumor cells. Interestingly, upstream analysis for the 40 genes identified by compare analysis revealed ZFPM1 (friend of GATA protein 1) as top transcription regulator. However, we did not observe any effect of triptolide to the binding of GATA1 in vitro. We confirmed that triptolide inhibited NF-kappaB activity, and it strongly bound to the pharmacophores of IkappaB kinase beta and NF-kappaB in silico. Conclusion Triptolide showed promising inhibitory effect toward NF-kappaB, making it a potential candidate for targeting NF-kappaB.
abstract_zh: 背景 雷公藤甲素（Triptolide）是一种活性天然产物，通过影响多种分子和信号通路（如caspases、热休克蛋白、DNA损伤和NF-kB），抑制细胞增殖、诱导细胞凋亡、抑制肿瘤转移，并在多种癌细胞系中增强其他治疗的效果。目的 我们研究了雷公藤甲素对NF-kB和GATA1的影响。方法 我们使用了细胞活力测定、基于微阵列的mRNA转录组全表达数据的比较和聚类分析、基因启动子结合基序分析、分子对接、Ingenuity通路分析、NF-kB报告细胞测定以及GATA1的电泳迁移率变动分析（EMSA）。结果 雷公藤甲素抑制了药物敏感（CCRF-CEM、U87.MG）和耐药细胞系（CEM/ADR5000、U87.MGDeltaEGFR）的生长。层次聚类分析显示树状图中有六个主要聚类。敏感和耐药细胞系的分布具有统计学显著性（p = 0.65 x 10(-2)）。NF-kappaB（Rel）和GATA1蛋白的结合基序在所有基因的25 kb上游启动子区域显著富集。IPA显示了影响雷公藤甲素对肿瘤细胞活性的网络、生物学功能和经典通路。有趣的是，通过比较分析识别的40个基因的上游分析揭示ZFPM1（GATA蛋白1的伙伴）为顶级转录调控因子。然而，我们未观察到雷公藤甲素对GATA1体外结合的任何影响。我们确认雷公藤甲素抑制了NF-kappaB活性，并在计算机模拟中强烈结合到IkappaB激酶β和NF-kappaB的药效团上。结论 雷公藤甲素对NF-kappaB显示出有前景的抑制效果，使其成为靶向NF-kappaB的潜在候选药物。
